title: Robustness of RKKY interactions across a Weyl node-annihilation transition
summary: Weyl semimetals (WSMs), with their unique topological properties and distinct electronic structure, exhibit intriguing properties when either time-reversal or inversion symmetries are broken. In this work, we consider the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction between magnetic impurities in time-reversal symmetry-breaking WSMs. We derive analytical expressions for the full RKKY exchange tensor in arbitrary two-band spinful lattice systems. Our approach reveals both Heisenberg, anisotropic Ising and Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya terms, which can be calculated by energy-integrating real-space Green's functions across the entire Brillouin zone, with the band edge acting as a natural energy cutoff. We apply this framework to study a two-band tight-binding model for a time-reversal symmetry-breaking WSM that interpolates between a Weyl phase with well-separated chiral nodes and a quadratic band-touching semimetal phase. Remarkably, the spatial profile, magnitude, and anisotropic tensor structure of the exchange couplings remain persistent across the node-annihilation transition. This topological robustness reveals that short- and intermediate-range RKKY interactions are mediated by the global, Brillouin-zone-integrated quantum metric of the full valence band rather than being strictly dictated by local low-energy Berry curvature monopoles. These findings demonstrate the necessity of full-band tight-binding formulations when predicting real-space magnetic interactions, providing key insights for electric-field tuning of magnetic anisotropy and constructing realistic models of heavy-fermion and Weyl-Kondo semimetals.

AI.tldr: This paper derives analytical expressions for the full RKKY exchange tensor in time-reversal symmetry-breaking Weyl semimetals using two-band spinful lattice models. It reveals that RKKY interactions (Heisenberg, Ising, and Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya terms) remain topologically robust across the Weyl-to-quadratic band-touching transition, as they are governed by the global Brillouin-zone-integrated quantum metric of the valence band rather than local Berry curvature monopoles.
AI.motivation: To understand how RKKY magnetic interactions behave in Weyl semimetals with broken time-reversal symmetry, and to determine whether these interactions are dictated by local topological features (Berry curvature monopoles at Weyl nodes) or by global band-structure properties across the full Brillouin zone.
AI.method: Derivation of analytical expressions for the full RKKY exchange tensor (including Heisenberg, anisotropic Ising, and Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya terms) for arbitrary two-band spinful lattice systems, using energy-integrated real-space Green's functions over the entire Brillouin zone. The framework is applied to a two-band tight-binding model of a time-reversal symmetry-breaking WSM that interpolates between a Weyl phase with separated chiral nodes and a quadratic band-touching semimetal phase.
AI.result: The spatial profile, magnitude, and anisotropic tensor structure of RKKY exchange couplings remain persistent across the node-annihilation (Weyl-to-quadratic band-touching) transition. Short- and intermediate-range RKKY interactions are mediated by the global, Brillouin-zone-integrated quantum metric of the full valence band, not by local Berry curvature monopoles at the Weyl nodes.
AI.conclusion: Full-band tight-binding formulations are essential for accurately predicting real-space magnetic interactions in topological semimetals. The findings provide key insights for electric-field tuning of magnetic anisotropy and for constructing realistic models of heavy-fermion and Weyl-Kondo semimetals.

title: Diffusion under competing bulk and surface stopping mechanisms
summary: We investigate reflected diffusion in a bounded domain subject to two independent, competing stopping mechanisms: an exponentially distributed bulk lifetime of rate $p$ and a surface reaction triggered when the boundary local time exceeds an independent exponential threshold of rate $q$. Denoting by $T$ the stopping time and by $L$ the acquired boundary local time at stopping, we derive their marginal distributions, joint Laplace transform, and complete hierarchy of mixed moments. These statistics are determined by the splitting probability $φ$ that surface reaction occurs before bulk decay. In particular, we establish the identity $p\expect{T}+q\expect{L}=1$ and show that the cumulative risk $pT+qL$ is exponentially distributed with unit rate. We further obtain equivalent representations of $φ$ in terms of the Robin-Laplacian and the generalized Steklov spectra. Explicit results for a three-dimensional ball reveal how competing rates $p,q$ control $φ$ and the $(T,L)$ statistics. Monte Carlo simulations test the universal cumulative-risk law.

AI.tldr: This paper studies reflected diffusion in a bounded domain with two competing stopping mechanisms: bulk decay (exponential rate p) and surface reaction triggered by boundary local time exceeding an exponential threshold (rate q). The authors derive the marginal distributions, joint Laplace transform, and mixed moments of the stopping time T and boundary local time L, establish that the cumulative risk pT+qL is exponentially distributed with unit rate, and express the splitting probability φ via Robin-Laplacian and generalized Steklov spectra, with explicit results for a 3D ball and Monte Carlo verification.
AI.motivation: The work aims to understand the statics of a reflected diffusion that can be stopped by either of two competing mechanisms—bulk degradation/decay and surface-induced reaction—which is relevant in physical and chemical settings where a particle diffusing in a bounded domain may react either in the bulk or upon encountering the boundary. Understanding the joint statistics of stopping time and boundary local time is essential for characterizing such competitive reaction-diffusion processes.
AI.method: The authors model the stopped reflected diffusion with an exponentially distributed bulk lifetime (rate p) and an independent exponential threshold (rate q) on boundary local time. They derive marginal distributions of T and L, the joint Laplace transform, and the full hierarchy of mixed moments, all expressed through the splitting probability φ that surface reaction occurs before bulk decay. They establish the identity p⟨T⟩+q⟨L⟩=1 and prove that the cumulative risk pT+qL is exponentially distributed with unit rate. They also derive equivalent spectral representations of φ using the Robin-Laplacian and generalized Steklov spectra, and provide explicit calculations for a three-dimensional ball.
AI.result: The paper yields closed-form statistics for (T,L), including the identity p⟨T⟩+q⟨L⟩=1 and the universal law that pT+qL is exponentially distributed with unit rate. Spectral representations of the splitting probability φ are obtained via Robin-Laplacian and generalized Steklov eigenvalues. Explicit results for a 3D ball demonstrate how the rates p and q control φ and the (T,L) statistics, and Monte Carlo simulations confirm the universal cumulative-risk law.
AI.conclusion: The two competing stopping mechanisms—bulk decay and surface reaction—lead to remarkably simple universal structure in the cumulative risk, namely that pT+qL is an exponential random variable of unit rate regardless of domain geometry. The splitting probability φ serves as the central governing quantity, expressible spectrally, and the framework provides a complete characterization of the (T,L) statistics for reflected diffusions in bounded domains.

title: Engineering Giant Thermoelectric Performance through Electrode-Coupling Geometry and Magnetic Flux in Quasiperiodic Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Rings
summary: We investigate coherent thermoelectric transport in magnetic-flux-threaded quasiperiodic Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) rings with engineered multi-site electrode couplings using the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism within the Landauer-Büttiker framework. We demonstrate that the electrode-coupling geometry serves as a powerful control parameter for tailoring quantum interference, thereby reshaping the transmission spectrum and thermoelectric response. In the absence of magnetic flux, the trivial dimerized phase ($t_1>t_2$) exhibits the highest thermoelectric efficiency, with asymmetric coupling producing a substantially larger figure of merit than the symmetric geometry. Magnetic flux further reconstructs the transmission spectrum through Aharonov-Bohm interference, driving a crossover of the optimal thermoelectric regime from the trivial to the topological dimerized phase. Under optimal flux conditions, the thermoelectric figure of merit reaches $ZT \approx 12$ for symmetric coupling and is dramatically enhanced to $ZT \approx 90$ for asymmetric coupling through enhanced energy filtering and suppressed electronic thermal transport. We further establish a clear correlation between the enhancement of thermoelectric efficiency and the violation of the Wiedemann-Franz law. Our results demonstrate that the combined interplay of quasiperiodicity, topology, magnetic flux, and electrode-coupling geometry provides a versatile strategy for engineering high-performance coherent thermoelectric devices.

Using the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism within the Landauer-Büttiker framework, the authors show that electrode-coupling geometry controls quantum interference and reshapes the transmission spectrum. Asymmetric coupling enhances the figure of merit (ZT≈90 vs ZT≈12 for symmetric coupling under optimal flux) compared to symmetric geometry, with magnetic flux driving a crossover of optimal thermoelectric performance from the trivial to the topological dimerized phase. Enhanced efficiency correlates with violation of the Wiedemann-Franz law.
AI.motivation: To develop versatile strategies for engineering high-performance coherent thermoelectric devices by understanding how the combined interplay of quasiperiodicity, topology, magnetic flux, and electrode-coupling geometry controls quantum interference and thermoelectric response in SSH rings.
AI.method: The study uses the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism within the Landauer-Büttiker framework to compute coherent thermoelectric transport in magnetic-flux-threaded quasiperiodic SSH rings. The electrode-coupling geometry (symmetric vs. asymmetric multi-site couplings) is systematically varied, and magnetic flux is introduced to reconstruct the transmission spectrum via Aharonov-Bohm interference.
AI.result: The electrode-coupling geometry reshapes the transmission spectrum and thermoelectric response. In the absence of flux, the trivial dimerized phase (t1>t2) yields the highest thermoelectric efficiency, with asymmetric coupling producing a substantially larger ZT than symmetric geometry. Magnetic flux drives a crossover of optimal performance from the trivial to the topological phase. Under optimal flux, ZT≈12 for symmetric coupling and ZT≈90 for asymmetric coupling, achieved via enhanced energy filtering and suppressed electronic thermal transport. Enhanced thermoelectric efficiency correlates with Wiedemann-Franz law violation.
AI.conclusion: The combined interplay of quasiperiodicity, topology, magnetic flux, and electrode-coupling geometry provides a versatile and powerful strategy for engineering high-performance coherent thermoelectric devices, with asymmetric coupling and magnetic flux enabling remarkably high thermoelectric figures of merit.

title: Non-reciprocally interacting Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes: Exceptional points, Anomalous relaxation, Pseudo-equilibrium and Boundary refrigeration
summary: Non-reciprocal interactions are ubiquitous in active, biological, and disordered systems, generically driving them out of equilibrium. Here, we introduce a hierarchy of non-reciprocally interacting Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (NROU) models governed by a tunable non-reciprocity parameter $g$. At a special point $g=g^*$, the drift matrix becomes non-diagonalizable, realizing exceptional points (EP's) of different orders, where eigenvalues and eigenvectors simultaneously coalesce. The hierarchy encompasses non-reciprocally coupled dimers, their disordered counterparts, and a many-body chain exactly mapping onto the paradigmatic Hatano-Nelson model in the arena of non-Hermitian quantum systems. For the disordered model, we show that the distribution of the EP location $g^*$ across disorder realizations develops a universal edge singularity precisely at the clean-system EP, and is manifestly non-self-averaging. Across all models, we find that at the EP, the usual exponential relaxation of the autocorrelation and covariance functions is dressed by a polynomial-in-time prefactor whose degree is set by the order of the EP and whose detailed structure encodes the spatial architecture of the chain. At complete asymmetry, the many-body chain exhibits ``pseudo-equilibrium'': its steady-state distribution factorizes into equilibrium-like single-particle measures despite a nonzero steady-state current. Moreover, the $N$-particle interacting system decomposes into $N/2$ independent complex OU processes. Finally, using the Harada-Sasa relation, we obtain a closed-form expression for the total steady-state heat dissipation and uncover a boundary refrigeration effect, in which the boundary particles switch from acting as a hot to a cold reservoir as the non-reciprocity is tuned.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a hierarchy of non-reciprocally interacting Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (NROU) models with a tunable non-reciprocity parameter g. At a critical point g*, exceptional points (EPs) of various orders form where eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce. The hierarchy spans dimers, disordered versions, and many-body chains mappable to the Hatano-Nelson model. Key findings include universal edge singularities in EP distributions, polynomial-in-time prefactors dressing exponential relaxation at EPs, a "pseudo-equilibrium" factorization at maximal asymmetry, a decomposition into independent complex OU processes, and a closed-form expression for heat dissipation revealing a boundary refrigeration effect.
AI.motivation: Non-reciprocal interactions are common in active, biological, and disordered systems and generically drive them out of equilibrium. The authors seek a tractable, analytically solvable class of models to systematically understand the role of non-reciprocity, exceptional points, and their consequences for relaxation dynamics, steady-state structure, and heat dissipation in such systems.
AI.method: The authors construct a hierarchy of NROU models whose drift matrix becomes non-diagonalizable at g=g*, yielding EPs of various orders. The hierarchy includes non-reciprocally coupled dimers, disordered variants, and a many-body chain exactly mapped to the Hatano-Nelson model. They analyze relaxation via autocorrelation/covariance functions, use the Harada-Sasa relation for heat dissipation, and study disorder via EP location distributions across realizations.
AI.result: The distribution of EP locations across disorder realizations shows a universal edge singularity at the clean-system EP and is non-self-averaging. At the EP, exponential relaxation is dressed by polynomial prefactors whose degree equals the EP order and structure encodes chain architecture. At complete asymmetry, the chain shows "pseudo-equilibrium" with factorized steady-state measures despite nonzero current, and the N-particle system splits into N/2 independent complex OU processes. The Harada-Sasa relation yields a closed-form total heat dissipation, revealing a boundary refrigeration effect where boundary particles switch between hot and cold reservoir roles with non-reciprocity tuning.
AI.conclusion: The NROU hierarchy provides a unifying, analytically tractable framework connecting exceptional points, non-reciprocal active and disordered systems, non-Hermitian quantum models, and stochastic thermodynamics. The results reveal universal signatures of EPs (polynomial relaxation prefactors, edge singularities in disorder), a novel pseudo-equilibrium steady state at maximal asymmetry, and observable thermodynamic consequences such as boundary refrigeration.

title: Electrostatic splitting of an Edge Magnetoplasmon Resonator
comment: Main text 10 pages and 7 figures, supplementary 6 pages and 10 figures
summary: Edge-magnetoplasmon resonators have been proposed as a powerful tool to detect anyons by introducing a quantum point contact into an isolated quantum Hall system probed via radiofrequency radiation. In this paper, we study the effect of a quantum point contact embedded within an edge-magnetoplasmon resonator and how its polarization influences the propagating magnetoplasmonic mode. Combining dc and rf measurements, we unambiguously evidence the signature of both integer ($ν= 1$ and $2$) and fractional quantum Hall states ($ν= 4/3$ and $2/3$) within the radiofrequency transmission signal. Using electrostatic gating, we determine the physical parameters characterizing the electrostatic edge of an AlGaAs/GaAs based two-dimensional electron gas. We extract the dependence of the cavity perimeter with the gate voltage of the quantum point contact and fully characterize the path followed by edge magnetoplasmons in this system. Finally, we provide a geometric model in good agreement with experimental results.

AI.tldr: The paper studies how a quantum point contact embedded in an edge-magnetoplasmon resonator affects propagating magnetoplasmonic modes. Combining dc and rf measurements, the authors demonstrate signatures of integer (ν=1,2) and fractional (ν=4/3, 2/3) quantum Hall states in the radiofrequency transmission signal. Using electrostatic gating, they characterize the electrostatic edge of an AlGaAs/GaAs 2DEG, extract the cavity perimeter dependence on gate voltage, and propose a geometric model matching experimental data.
AI.motivation: Edge-magnetoplasmon resonators with embedded quantum point contacts have been proposed as a tool for detecting anyons, and understanding how the QPC's electrostatic polarization affects magnetoplasmon propagation is essential for realizing such detection schemes.
AI.method: The authors perform simultaneous DC and radiofrequency transmission measurements on an edge-magnetoplasmon resonator with an embedded quantum point contact in an AlGaAs/GaAs two-dimensional electron gas. Electrostatic gating is used to tune the system, and the data is compared against a geometric model describing the edge-magnetoplasmon path.
AI.result: Clear signatures of integer (ν=1,2) and fractional (ν=4/3, 2/3) quantum Hall states are observed in the rf transmission. The cavity perimeter is extracted as a function of QPC gate voltage, and the edge trajectory is fully characterized. A geometric model reproduces the experimental observations well.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a detailed characterization of edge magnetoplasmon propagation through a QPC-embedded resonator, establishing a firm experimental foundation for future anyon detection schemes based on this platform.

title: Field-Driven Coupled Magnon--Phonon--Electron Relaxation in Magnetite Using Steepest-Entropy-Ascent Quantum Thermodynamic Formalism
summary: A field-driven steepest-entropy-ascent quantum thermodynamic (SEAQT) formulation is developed for longitudinal nonequilibrium relaxation in magnetite (Fe$_3$O$_4$) with coupled electron, phonon, and magnon populations. Material-specific excitation spectra define the thermodynamic state space, while one relaxation parameter for each population sets its kinetic scale. A longitudinal magnetic field shifts the dressed magnon eigenenergies while the occupation basis remains fixed; irreversible redistribution conserves instantaneous energy and electron number while allowing the magnon population to vary. The formulation yields nonequilibrium subsystem temperatures, entropy production, magnetic-work identities, and a coupled small-signal susceptibility incorporating energy-conservation feedback among all three populations; the one-pole Debye response appears only as a limiting case. Numerical results under sinusoidal driving show a transition from nearly quasistatic behavior to frequency-dependent lag, finite-amplitude departure from the linear-response ellipse, and increasing higher-harmonic content. Relaxational work per cycle increases strongly with field amplitude and frequency, while the complex susceptibility is broader and shifted relative to a Debye reference. Entropy production remains positive, and the electron, phonon, and magnon temperatures show distinct excursions followed by secular heating when positive magnetic work is retained without heat rejection. The calculated work represents longitudinal magnon quasiparticle relaxation in a homogeneous single-domain model, not the total core loss of a finite ferrite specimen.

AI.tldr: A field-driven steepest-entropy-ascent quantum thermodynamic (SEAQT) formulation is developed to model longitudinal nonequilibrium relaxation in magnetite (Fe3O4) with coupled electron, phonon, and magnon populations. The model yields nonequilibrium temperatures, entropy production, magnetic-work identities, and a coupled small-signal complex susceptibility. Numerical results under sinusoidal driving show transitions from quasistatic to frequency-dependent behavior with higher-harmonic content and strong increases in relaxational work per cycle with field amplitude and frequency.
AI.motivation: To develop a thermodynamically consistent nonequilibrium framework that captures coupled electron-phonon-magnon relaxation dynamics in magnetite under longitudinal magnetic fields, going beyond the limiting Debye single-pole response and linear-response approximations.
AI.method: A field-driven steepest-entropy-ascent quantum thermodynamic (SEAQT) formulation where material-specific excitation spectra define the thermodynamic state space, one relaxation parameter per population sets kinetic scales, and a longitudinal magnetic field shifts dressed magnon eigenenergies while the occupation basis remains fixed. Irreversible redistribution conserves instantaneous energy and electron number while allowing magnon population variation.
AI.result: The formulation predicts nonequilibrium subsystem temperatures, positive entropy production, and a coupled small-signal susceptibility with energy-conservation feedback. Under sinusoidal driving, results show a transition from quasistatic behavior to frequency-dependent lag, finite-amplitude deviations from linear-response ellipses, stronger higher-harmonic content, and relaxational work per cycle that increases strongly with both field amplitude and frequency. The complex susceptibility is broader and shifted relative to a Debye reference, with distinct electron/phonon/magnon temperature excursions and secular heating under retained positive magnetic work.
AI.conclusion: The SEAQT formulation provides a more general nonequilibrium thermodynamic treatment of longitudinal magnon relaxation in magnetite than the Debye or linear-response limits, capturing coupled population dynamics and field-amplitude-dependent behavior. title: Challenges in orbital current-driven domain wall motion in light metal/ferrimagnet heterostructures
comment: 24 pages, 6 figures. Published in Journal of Applied Physics
summary: Recent advances in spintronics suggest that orbital Hall currents generated by charge injection in light metals can provide nonequilibrium angular momentum without relying on strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC). Here, we examine whether such orbital currents can drive domain wall (DW) motion in an amorphous ferrimagnetic alloy, Gd$_{25}$(Fe$_{9}$Co$_{1}$)$_{75}$ (GFC), where the rare-earth sublattice offers strong SOC for orbital-to-spin conversion. We compare three representative heterostructures: Pt/GFC as a spin Hall reference, light-metal (Mn or Ti)/GFC for direct orbital-current injection, and light-metal/Pt/GFC incorporating an ultrathin Pt layer for orbital-to-spin conversion. Whereas Pt/GFC exhibits robust and reproducible spin-orbit-torque-driven DW motion, no current-driven DW motion is detected in Mn/GFC or Ti/GFC. Second-harmonic Hall measurements nevertheless reveal finite damping-like torques in both Mn/GFC and Ti/GFC, demonstrating that angular-momentum transfer into GFC does occur but is far weaker than in Pt/GFC. Inserting a 1-nm-thick Pt conversion layer strongly enhances the damping-like torque and restores DW motion. Thickness-dependent analysis further shows that DW mobility and depinning thresholds correlate with the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and domain-wall width, highlighting weak torque conversion and insufficient interfacial stabilization of chiral DWs as key challenges for orbital-driven DW motion in light-metal/ferrimagnet heterostructures.

While Pt/GFC heterostructures show robust spin-orbit-torque-driven DW motion, Mn/GFC and Ti/GFC show no current-driven DW motion despite finite damping-like torques. Inserting a 1-nm Pt conversion layer restores DW motion. The study identifies weak torque conversion and insufficient interfacial stabilization of chiral DWs as key limitations for orbital-current-driven DW motion in light-metal/ferrimagnet systems.

AI.method: Comparison of three heterostructure types—Pt/GFC (spin Hall reference), light-metal (Mn or Ti)/GFC (direct orbital-current injection), and light-metal/Pt/GFC (with ultrathin Pt for orbital-to-spin conversion)—using current-driven DW motion measurements and second-harmonic Hall for torque detection, along with thickness-dependent analysis of DW mobility and depinning thresholds correlated with interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction.

Adding a 1-nm Pt layer enhances damping-like torque and restores DW motion. DW mobility and depinning thresholds correlate with interfacial DMI and DW width.

The key challenges for orbital-driven DW motion are weak torque conversion and insufficient interfacial stabilization of chiral DWs in light-metal/ferrimagnet heterostructures.

title: Variable Charge State, Magnetic Excitations, and Kondo Effect of Sm/g/Ir(111)
summary: Using low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy we investigate the charge state, magnetic excitations, and Kondo features of individual Sm adatoms on graphene/Ir(111). Depending on the number and distance of their neighbors, Sm atoms can be in two discrete charge states. At certain distances, a reversible transition between these two states is induced by the electric field of the STM tip leading to concentric charge rings in the images. Only atoms in one of the two charge states exhibit magnetic excitations in d$I$/d$V$ spectra. Two such excitations are located at 35~meV and 54~meV and related to transitions from the $J = 1/2$ ground state doublet to the first crystal field split $J = 3/2$ multiplet. Together with the intra-atomic exchange excitations at higher energy, these observations indicate that Sm transfers one $6s$ electron to the substrate while it retains its gas-phase $4f$ filling. New for lanthanide adatoms, we observe a Kondo resonance. The Zeeman splitting of the Kondo peak reveals that Sm retains its large gas-phase $g$-factor. Comparison of d$I$/d$V$ spectra to cotunneling theory yields the crystal field acting on the $4f$ shell and, consequently, on the $J = 3/2$ quadruplet, confirms Sm$^+$ as the ground state, and identifies Sm$^{2+}$ as being energetically close, thereby rationalizing our observation of variable charge states.

AI.tldr: Using low-temperature STM on graphene/Ir(111), individual Sm adatoms exhibit two discrete charge states (Sm+ and Sm2+) depending on neighbor distance, with STM tip electric fields inducing reversible transitions between them. Only one charge state shows magnetic excitations at 35 and 54 meV (crystal field transitions within the J=3/2 multiplet). Samarium transfers one 6s electron to the substrate while retaining its 4f gas-phase filling, and a Kondo resonance is observed (novel for lanthanide adatoms) whose Zeeman splitting confirms the large atomic g-factor. Cotunneling theory comparison reveals the crystal field and rationalizes the proximity of Sm+ and Sm2+ ground states.
AI.motivation: To understand the electronic structure, magnetic properties, charge state variability, and Kondo physics of individual lanthanide (Sm) adatoms on a graphene/Ir(111) substrate, with particular interest in how adsorption environment tunes charge and magnetic behavior.
AI.method: Low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and scanning tunneling spectroscopy (dI/dV) to probe charge state, magnetic excitations, and Kondo features of individual Sm adatoms on graphene/Ir(111). Spectra are compared to cotunneling theory to extract the crystal field acting on the 4f shell and determine the ground-state configuration.
AI.result: Sm adatoms exist in two discrete charge states controllable by neighbor arrangement; STM tip field drives reversible transitions generating concentric charge rings. Only one charge state shows magnetic excitations at 35 and 54 meV assigned to J=1/2 to J=3/2 crystal field transitions. A Kondo resonance—novel for lanthanide adatoms—exhibits Zeeman splitting retaining the atomic g-factor. Cotunneling analysis yields the crystal field, confirms Sm+ ground state, and shows Sm2+ is energetically close.
AI.conclusion: Sm adatoms on graphene/Ir(111) transfer one 6s electron (Sm+) while preserving the 4f6 gas-phase configuration. The near-degeneracy of Sm+ and Sm2+ explains the observed charge bistability, and the crystal field acting on the 4f shell governs the magnetic excitations and Kondo behavior.

title: Multi-task deep-learning optimization of trade-off properties for superior-performance Fe-based soft magnetic alloys
comment: 92 pages, 8 main-text figures, 1 main-text table; Supplementary Materials included
summary: Fe-based amorphous alloys are promising soft magnetic materials for developing next-generation devices with high frequency and efficiency. However, optimization of Fe-based alloys with ultra-high saturation magnetic flux density (B_s), ultra-low coercivity (H_c), and good glass-forming ability is a notorious problem, owing to the vast composition space and complex trade-offs of these properties. Thus, conventional design methods encounter great challenges. Here we develop a generative multi-task deep learning (GMTDL) to achieve simultaneous optimization of compositions and trade-off properties. The GMTDL can sufficiently exploit and share the knowledge of datasets across different tasks, despite the limitation and imbalance of these datasets. Therefore, it exhibits superior performance in prediction of alloys with multiple targeted properties, outperforming previous machine learning-based design strategies. Moreover, the GMTDL can also tailor compositions, providing an efficient way to regulate properties and generate desired candidates for further experimental processing. The validity and reliability of GMTDL are rigorously tested by benchmarking with Fe-based alloys reported very recently. Moreover, some new alloys with ultra-high B_s and ultra-low H_c are predicted. The optimal content windows of key elements and their synergistic effects are also unraveled for practical guidance. Thus, our study establishes an effective and reliable paradigm for simultaneous prediction and optimization of high-performance materials with multiple properties.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a generative multi-task deep learning (GMTDL) framework to simultaneously optimize Fe-based amorphous alloys for high saturation magnetic flux density (B_s), low coercivity (H_c), and good glass-forming ability, overcoming the challenges of vast composition spaces and property trade-offs that conventional methods cannot handle.
AI.motivation: Fe-based amorphous alloys are promising for high-frequency, high-efficiency devices, but achieving simultaneous optimization of ultra-high B_s, ultra-low H_c, and good glass-forming ability is notoriously difficult due to the vast composition space and complex property trade-offs, making conventional design methods inadequate.
AI.method: A generative multi-task deep learning (GMTDL) framework is developed that exploits and shares knowledge across datasets of different tasks, despite dataset limitations and imbalances. It performs simultaneous optimization of compositions and trade-off properties, can tailor compositions to regulate properties, and generate candidate alloys for experimental validation.
AI.result: GMTDL outperforms previous machine learning-based design strategies in predicting alloys with multiple targeted properties. Its validity was confirmed by benchmarking against recently reported Fe-based alloys, and it successfully predicted new alloys with ultra-high B_s and ultra-low H_c. The optimal content windows of key elements and their synergistic effects were also unraveled.
AI.conclusion: The study establishes an effective and reliable paradigm for simultaneous prediction and optimization of high-performance materials with multiple properties, providing practical guidance for developing advanced Fe-based amorphous alloys.

title: Local coordination, structural softening, and polarization-switching energetics in Sc-alloyed GaN
summary: Sc-alloyed wurtzite nitrides exhibit strongly tunable electromechanical and ferroelectric properties, yet the relationship between their lattice evolution and local bonding environment remains insufficiently established, particularly in Sc$_x$Ga$_{1-x}$N. Here, we investigate the structural and local bonding evolution of Sc$_x$Ga$_{1-x}$N across the dilute-to-intermediate composition range by combining X-ray diffraction, Sc K-edge X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES), extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) and first-principles calculations. Sc incorporation produces an anisotropic lattice expansion and a progressive reduction in the c/a ratio. XANES and EXAFS reveal a concurrent modification of the local environment around Sc, with the effective Sc-N coordination number increasing from 4.1(4) to 4.5(2) and the average Sc-N bond length increasing from 2.045(7) to 2.081(8)Å over x=0.06-0.26. The local response is accompanied by a reduction in the Sc K-edge pre-edge intensity, consistent with a gradual reduction of the local tetrahedral asymmetry. First-principles calculations show that these structural changes are associated with site-selective distortions around Sc and progressive flattening of the structural energy landscape. The calculated intrinsic polarization-switching barrier decreases from 24.2 to 19.0 meV/Å$^3$ with increasing Sc content, while the calculated piezoelectric stress coefficient (e$_{33}$) increases from 0.82 to 1.66~C/m$^2$ and elastic constant (C$_{33}$) decreases from 380 to 227~GPa, resulting in an increase of piezoelectric strain coefficient (d$_{33}$) from 2.99 to 12.46~pC/N. These results show that Sc incorporation progressively modifies the local coordination environment and structural energetics of ScGaN while the long-range wurtzite structure remains preserved over the investigated composition range.

AI.tldr: This study combines XRD, XANES, EXAFS, and first-principles calculations to elucidate how Sc incorporation in wurtzite ScxGa1-xN alters both the lattice and local bonding environment, showing progressive increases in Sc-N coordination number and bond length, reduced local tetrahedral asymmetry, lower polarization-switching barriers, and enhanced piezoelectric response while preserving the wurtzite structure.
AI.motivation: Sc-alloyed wurtzite nitrides have strongly tunable electromechanical and ferroelectric properties, but the relationship between lattice evolution and local bonding environment in ScxGa1-xN remains insufficiently understood, especially across the dilute-to-intermediate composition range.
AI.method: The authors employ a multi-technique approach combining X-ray diffraction for long-range structural analysis, Sc K-edge XANES and EXAFS for local environment probing, and first-principles calculations to connect the observed structural and bonding changes to macroscopic electromechanical properties.
AI.result: Sc incorporation yields anisotropic lattice expansion and reduced c/a ratio. The Sc-N coordination number rises from 4.1(4) to 4.5(2), bond length from 2.045(7) to 2.081(8) Å (x=0.06-0.26), with reduced pre-edge intensity indicating diminished tetrahedral asymmetry. Calculations reveal a decrease in switching barrier from 24.2 to 19.0 meV/Å³, increase in e33 from 0.82 to 1.66 C/m² and d33 from 2.99 to 12.46 pC/N, while C33 decreases from 380 to 227 GPa.
AI.conclusion: Sc incorporation progressively modifies the local coordination environment and structural energetics while the long-range wurtzite structure is preserved over the investigated composition range, providing mechanistic insight into the enhanced piezoelectric and ferroelectric response of ScGaN.

title: Influence of dislocation density on the tribological response in oxides: case study on SrTiO3
summary: Most ceramics suffer from brittle surface damage and cracking when small particles slide across the surface under low load. Microscratching tests are a useful technique to mimic this loading scenario while retaining the material's deformation history; however, the impact of pre-seeded dislocations, which can significantly facilitate plastic deformation, has not been explored in ceramics. Here, the influence of mechanically seeded dislocations on the microscratching response of oxides is investigated using a model perovskite, SrTiO3. First, various dislocation densities over four orders of magnitude are introduced via room-temperature cyclic Brinell indenter scratching. Subsequently, load-ramped microscratching tests are performed within the pristine and dislocation-seeded regions using a nominally 30 μm spherical diamond tip. On the reference pristine surface, we observe a clear transition from elastic to elasto-plastic deformation, followed by median/radial cracking at higher loads. In contrast, pre-seeded dislocations, accompanied by residual compressive stresses, suppress elastic deformation and lead to median/radial crack shortening and subsequent transition to a partial cone crack. The subsurface cracks are characterized by 3D Nano-CT. The changes in crack geometry, with and without dislocations, were described using the Lawn-Evans-Marshall and Lawn-Wiederhorn-Roberts models. These findings provide direct evidence of dislocation-regulated near-surface damage tolerance, with general applicability to other plastically deformable oxides.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how mechanically seeded dislocations influence the microscratching response of oxide ceramics using SrTiO3 as a model perovskite. Pre-seeded dislocations suppress elastic deformation, shorten median/radial cracks, and promote a transition to partial cone cracks, demonstrating dislocation-regulated near-surface damage tolerance with general applicability to other plastically deformable oxides.
AI.motivation: Most ceramics suffer brittle surface damage when small particles slide across under low load. While microscratching tests mimic this loading scenario, the influence of pre-seeded dislocations—which could significantly facilitate plastic deformation—on the microscratching response of ceramics has not been previously explored.
AI.method: Dislocation densities spanning four orders of magnitude were introduced into SrTiO3 via room-temperature cyclic Brinell indenter scratching. Load-ramped microscratching tests were then performed in pristine and dislocation-seeded regions using a 30 μm spherical diamond tip. Subsurface cracks were characterized by 3D Nano-CT, and crack geometry changes were analyzed using Lawn-Evans-Marshall and Lawn-Wiederhorn-Roberts models.
AI.result: Pristine surfaces showed a clear elastic-to-elasto-plastic transition followed by median/radial cracking at higher loads. Pre-seeded dislocations with residual compressive stresses suppressed elastic deformation, shortened median/radial cracks, and induced a transition to partial cone cracks.
AI.conclusion: The findings provide direct evidence of dislocation-regulated near-surface damage tolerance in ceramics, with general applicability to other plastically deformable oxides.

title: Generalized Helicity-Dependent Magnetization Switching via Substrate Phonons
summary: Coherent excitation of circularly-polarized substrate phonons can drive deterministic reversal of magnetization in an adjacent magnetic layer. However, the extent to which this substrate-mediated mechanism can be generalized across different materials remains unresolved. Here, we measure and compare the spectral dependence of helicity-dependent magnetization reversal in magnetic GdFeCo layers grown on a diverse set of diamagnetic substrates. Switching is observed for all investigated substrates, spanning six point groups and several infrared-active transverse-optical phonon symmetries. While the switching spectra broadly overlap with the Reststrahlen bands, their maxima are systematically shifted to wavelengths shorter than the corresponding transverse-optical phonon resonances. This spectral mismatch shows that substrate absorption alone does not determine the switching efficiency. Transfer-matrix calculations show that strong absorption concentrates energy deposition near the substrate interface, providing a possible source of local heating that could suppress magnetization reversal. Our results reveal the broad applicability of substrate-mediated phononic switching while showing that its efficiency is governed by the full optical response of the heterostructure rather than substrate absorption alone.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the generality of substrate-mediated phononic magnetization reversal by measuring helicity-dependent switching in magnetic GdFeCo layers grown on diverse diamagnetic substrates. Switching occurs across all substrates spanning six point groups, but the switching spectra are systematically blue-shifted relative to substrate phonon resonances, revealing that efficiency is governed by the full optical response of the heterostructure, not substrate absorption alone.
AI.motivation: Coherent excitation of circularly-polarized substrate phonons can drive deterministic magnetization reversal in adjacent magnetic layers, but the extent to which this substrate-mediated mechanism generalizes across different materials was unresolved. The authors aim to determine whether this switching mechanism is broadly applicable or limited to specific substrate classes.
AI.method: The authors measured and compared the spectral dependence of helicity-dependent magnetization reversal in magnetic GdFeCo layers grown on a diverse set of diamagnetic substrates, spanning six point groups with various infrared-active transverse-optical phonon symmetries. They correlated switching spectra with Reststrahlen bands and used transfer-matrix calculations to analyze energy deposition profiles near the substrate interface.
AI.result: Switching was observed for all investigated substrates. While switching spectra broadly overlap with Reststrahlen bands, their maxima are systematically shifted to shorter wavelengths than the transverse-optical phonon resonances. Transfer-matrix calculations showed that strong substrate absorption concentrates energy deposition near the substrate interface, potentially causing local heating that suppresses magnetization reversal.
AI.conclusion: Substrate-mediated phononic switching is broadly applicable across diverse diamagnetic substrates, but its efficiency is determined by the full optical response of the heterostructure rather than substrate absorption alone. The observed spectral mismatch relative to phonon resonances highlights the role of local heating in governing switching efficiency.

title: A locally ab initio computational framework for arbitrary incommensurate materials interfaces
summary: Incommensurate materials interfaces constitute a broad and technologically important class of systems, yet their lack of shared periodicity limits predictive and computationally efficient first-principles electronic-structure methods. Here we introduce a scalable computational framework for constructing locally ab initio electronic Hamiltonians for arbitrary materials interfaces. Our approach exploits the nearsightedness of Wannier Hamiltonian matrix elements, enabling their systematic extrapolation and interpolation across interlayer registries. This strategy yields transferable Hamiltonians that retain first-principles accuracy while bypassing the need for prohibitively large commensurate supercells or Moiré approximations. We validate the framework on quasicrystalline 30° twisted bilayer graphene, reproducing experimentally observed spectral features including mirrored Dirac cones and minigaps at avoided crossings arising from generalized interlayer scattering. We further predict quasiperiodic flat-band states in experimentally accessible doping regimes. By enabling predictive electronic-structure calculations across structurally incommensurate interfaces, this framework establishes a practical route to first-principles exploration of emergent interfacial phenomena.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a scalable computational framework for constructing locally ab initio electronic Hamiltonians at arbitrary incommensurate materials interfaces by exploiting the nearsightedness of Wannier Hamiltonian matrix elements, enabling extrapolation and interpolation across interlayer registries. The method avoids large commensurate supercells or Moiré approximations, and is validated on quasicrystalline 30° twisted bilayer graphene where it reproduces mirrored Dirac cones, minigaps at avoided crossings, and predicts quasiperiodic flat bands in experimentally accessible doping regimes.
AI.motivation: Incommensurate materials interfaces are technologically important but lack shared periodicity, which limits predictive and computationally efficient first-principles electronic-structure methods. Standard approaches require prohibitively large commensurate supercells or rely on Moiré approximations.
AI.method: The framework exploits the nearsightedness (short-range spatial decay) of Wannier Hamiltonian matrix elements to systematically extrapolate and interpolate them across different interlayer registries, producing transferable local Hamiltonians that retain first-principles accuracy without needing commensurate supercells.
AI.result: Validation on quasicrystalline 30° twisted bilayer graphene reproduces experimentally observed spectral features including mirrored Dirac cones and minigaps at avoided crossings from generalized interlayer scattering. The method also predicts quasiperiodic flat-band states in experimentally accessible doping regimes.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables predictive first-principles electronic-structure calculations across structurally incommensurate interfaces, establishing a practical route to explore emergent interfacial phenomena computationally.

title: Cross-Layer Anomalous Hall Transport driven by Néel-Vector rotating in the Altermagnet candidate V2Te2O
summary: In van der Waals (vdW) materials, weak interlayer coupling generally suppresses vertical dispersion, reinforcing the conventional paradigm that in-plane transport dominates over cross-layer channels. Here, using first-principles calculations and magnetic symmetry analyses, we uncover a giant, symmetry-unlocked cross-layer anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) in the vdW altermagnet V2Te2O. In the magnetic ground state with Neel vector N//z, horizontal mirror symmetry protects a spin-polarized nodal chain near the Fermi level and strictly enforces zero anomalous Hall response. Tilting the Neel vector explicitly breaks this mirror protection, allowing spin-orbit coupling to gap the nodal chain and activate a sharp cross-layer Hall response. When the Neel vector is rotated into the in-plane configuration (N//x), cross-layer orbital hybridization generates intensive Berry curvature hotspots, boosting the cross-layer component of AHC σ_{yz} to approximately 255 S/cm, which exceeds in-plane component σ_{xy} by nearly two orders of magnitude. Furthermore, varying the azimuthal angle systematically redistributes the anomalous Hall response, enabling full directional control of transverse transport. Our findings demonstrate a highly sensitive cross-layer anomalous Hall switch activated by low-barrier spin canting, offering promising avenues for directional tensor selection and low-power multi-axial vdW spintronics.

AI.tldr: The paper reveals a giant cross-layer anomalous Hall conductivity in the van der Waals altermagnet V2Te2O, where rotating the Neel vector from out-of-plane to in-plane breaks mirror symmetry protection, activates spin-orbit coupling gaps in a nodal chain, and boosts the cross-layer AHC to ~255 S/cm—nearly two orders of magnitude larger than the in-plane component—enabling a low-barrier, directionally controllable anomalous Hall switch for multi-axial vdW spintronics.
AI.motivation: Conventional paradigms hold that weak interlayer coupling in vdW materials suppresses vertical dispersion and cross-layer transport. The authors aim to challenge this assumption and explore whether symmetry-controlled cross-layer anomalous Hall effects can be achieved in vdW magnetic materials, potentially enabling new functional spintronic devices.
AI.method: First-principles density functional theory calculations combined with magnetic symmetry analysis are employed to study the altermagnet V2Te2O. The analysis focuses on how Neel vector orientation affects mirror symmetry protection of a spin-polarized nodal chain, spin-orbit coupling-induced gap opening, Berry curvature distributions, and the resulting anomalous Hall conductivity tensor components.
AI.result: When the Neel vector is along z, horizontal mirror symmetry enforces zero anomalous Hall response despite a spin-polarized nodal chain near the Fermi level. Tilting the Neel vector breaks mirror protection and activates a sharp cross-layer Hall response via SOC gap opening. For the in-plane Neel vector N//x, orbital hybridization creates intensive Berry curvature hotspots, yielding a cross-layer AHC σ_{yz} ≈ 255 S/cm—exceeding the in-plane σ_{xy} by roughly two orders of magnitude. Azimuthal angle variation enables systematic redistribution and full directional control of the Hall response.
AI.conclusion: The work demonstrates a highly responsive cross-layer anomalous Hall switch actuated by low-barrier spin canting, establishing vdW altermagnets as viable platforms for directional tensor selection and low-power multi-axial spintronic applications, while fundamentally revising the notion that interlayer transport is always suppressed in vdW systems.

title: Anharmonic Lattice Dynamics and Anisotropic Electron-Phonon Coupling in Quasi-1-Dimensional Charge Density Wave Ta2NiSe7
summary: The microscopic origin of charge density wave formation in quasi one dimensional Ta2NiSe7 remains actively debated, particularly regarding the relative contributions of Fermi surface nesting, electron phonon coupling, and lattice instabilities. Here, we combine temperature and orientation dependent polarized Raman spectroscopy with first principles calculations to uncover the anisotropic electronic and lattice interactions governing the CDW state in Ta2NiSe7. Heat capacity and electrical transport measurements identify an incommensurate CDW transition at 61 K. Raman spectroscopy reveals pronounced in plane anisotropy, with e ph coupling strength along intrachain b axis exceeding five times that along interchain c axis, whereas lattice anharmonicity is enhanced by threefold along c axis. First principles calculations identify Ta2 Se octahedral vibrations and Ta Se electronic states near the Fermi level as dominant channels mediating the anisotropic e ph interaction. Exceptionally strong and directional e ph coupling along b axis establishes lattice driven electronic instability as the primary mechanism underlying CDW modulation and highlights the dominance of intrachain interactions in strongly coupled Ta2NiSe7. Despite this strong coupling, the CDW remains incommensurate, indicating that lattice anharmonicity provides an additional degree of freedom. Enhanced anharmonicity along c axis suggests that anisotropic phonon phonon interactions reshape the free energy landscape and contribute to stabilizing incommensurate phase. These findings reveal a cooperative interplay between anisotropic e ph coupling and lattice anharmonicity in governing CDW formation in low dimensional quantum materials.

AI.tldr: This study combines temperature- and orientation-dependent polarized Raman spectroscopy with first-principles calculations to investigate charge density wave (CDW) formation in quasi-1D Ta2NiSe7. The CDW transition occurs at 61 K and is incommensurate. Strong anisotropic electron-phonon coupling (5x stronger along the intrachain b-axis than interchain c-axis) drives the CDW, while 3x-enhanced lattice anharmonicity along the c-axis contributes to stabilizing the incommensurate phase through reshaped free energy landscape.
AI.motivation: The microscopic origin of CDW formation in quasi-1D Ta2NiSe7 is debated, particularly regarding the relative contributions of Fermi surface nesting, electron-phonon coupling, and lattice instabilities. Understanding this mechanism requires disentangling the anisotropic electronic and lattice interactions governing the CDW state.
AI.method: Combined temperature- and orientation-dependent polarized Raman spectroscopy with first-principles calculations, supplemented by heat capacity and electrical transport measurements to characterize the CDW transition and anisotropic interactions.
AI.result: An incommensurate CDW transition occurs at 61 K. Raman spectroscopy reveals pronounced in-plane anisotropy: electron-phonon coupling strength along the intrachain b-axis exceeds that along interchain c-axis by more than 5x, while lattice anharmonicity is enhanced 3x along the c-axis. First-principles calculations identify Ta2Se octahedral vibrations and Ta-Se electronic states near the Fermi level as the dominant channels mediating anisotropic e-ph interaction.
AI.conclusion: Lattice-driven electronic instability, enabled by exceptionally strong and directional electron-phonon coupling along the b-axis, is the primary mechanism underlying CDW modulation, highlighting the dominance of intrachain interactions. The incommensurate nature of the CDW, despite strong coupling, indicates that anisotropy in lattice anharmonicity reshapes the free energy landscape and helps stabilize the incommensurate phase, revealing a cooperative interplay between anisotropic e-ph coupling and lattice anharmonicity in low-dimensional CDW materials.

title: Semiclassical thermoelectric transport in disordered Dirac electron system Ag2Te
summary: We investigated the thermoelectric effects of the Dirac electron system Ag2Te under magnetic field. Our anal-ysis based on the Boltzmann semiclassical model associated the disorder with the unconventional magnetic field responses such as linear magnetoresistance, linear Nernst effect, step-like Nernst effect, and sign change in Nernst effect. The analysis also revealed the impurity band near the Fermi energy. We simultaneously clari-fied the serious impact of the thermal Hall effect on the measurement of the Nernst effect, and we proposed the definitive solution. Our careful measurement and analysis will be the standard for the thermoelectric study under magnetic field.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates thermoelectric effects in the Dirac electron system Ag2Te under magnetic fields, using Boltzmann semiclassical analysis to link disorder with unconventional magnetic field responses including linear magnetoresistance, linear and step-like Nernst effects, and sign changes in the Nernst effect. It also identifies an impurity band near the Fermi energy, reveals the thermal Hall effect's contamination of Nernst measurements, and proposes a definitive correction method.
AI.motivation: To understand the unconventional thermoelectric and magnetotransport responses in Dirac electron systems like Ag2Te under magnetic fields, and to address measurement artifacts (thermal Hall contamination) that compromise accurate Nernst effect characterization.
AI.method: Experimental measurements of thermoelectric effects in Ag2Te under magnetic field, combined with theoretical analysis based on the Boltzmann semiclassical model that incorporates disorder to explain the observed magnetoresistance and Nernst behavior.
AI.result: Disorder was identified as the origin of linear magnetoresistance, linear Nernst effect, step-like Nernst effect, and sign changes in the Nernst effect. An impurity band near the Fermi energy was revealed, and the thermal Hall effect was shown to seriously contaminate Nernst measurements, with a definitive solution proposed.
AI.conclusion: The combination of careful measurement and disorder-based semiclassical analysis provides a standard framework for thermoelectric studies under magnetic fields, resolving both the physical origin of anomalous responses and the measurement complications arising from thermal Hall contamination.

title: Interfacial Accommodation as a Candidate Ductility Pathway in Intermetallic-Rich Alloys
summary: Heterophase interfaces are increasingly recognized as active participants in plastic deformation, yet quantitative methods for comparing their strain-accommodation capacity remain limited. Here, we present an atomistic framework for quantifying interface-mediated strain accommodation using molecular dynamics simulations. Interface broadening, roughening, and migration are extracted from atomistic trajectories and combined into an Interface Accommodation Index, with a normalized counterpart accounting for differences in initial interface structure. A weighting sensitivity analysis demonstrates that the relative ranking of interfaces is robust to the specific form of the index. The framework is demonstrated for three experimentally motivated interfaces, Al/Al3Ti, Al/Al9M2, and Al9M2/Al3Ti (M = Fe, Co, Ni), under tensile, compressive, and shear loading. Bulk simulations show that Shockley partial dislocations dominate plastic deformation, with alloy chemistry governing the transition toward mixed-character dislocation networks. Tensile loading produces the greatest interface accommodation, while shear produces comparatively limited structural evolution. The Al9M2/Al3Ti interface exhibits both the highest yield resistance and the largest accommodation response, suggesting that intermetallic-intermetallic interfaces can simultaneously sustain load and redistribute strain. These simulations quantify structural accommodation rather than ductility or fracture directly; their connection to macroscopic ductility therefore requires experimental validation. The framework provides a transferable approach for comparing interface accommodation in multiphase alloys and identifies interface chemistry and crystallography as important design variables for damage-tolerant structural materials.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an atomistic framework using molecular dynamics simulations to quantify interface-mediated strain accommodation in heterophase interfaces. It introduces an Interface Accommodation Index (and normalized counterpart) that combines interface broadening, roughening, and migration metrics. Demonstrated on Al/Al3Ti, Al/Al9M2, and Al9M2/Al3Ti (M = Fe, Co, Ni) interfaces under various loading conditions, the framework reveals that tensile loading maximally activates interface accommodation, intermetallic-intermetallic interfaces (Al9M2/Al3Ti) offer both high yield resistance and large accommodation response, and the ranking is robust to index formulation.
AI.motivation: Heterophase interfaces are known contributors to plastic deformation, but quantitative methods to compare their strain-accommodation capacity across different interfaces are lacking, limiting rational interface design in multiphase alloys.
AI.method: Molecular dynamics simulations are used to extract interface broadening, roughening, and migration from atomistic trajectories, which are then combined into an Interface Accommodation Index with a normalized version accounting for differences in initial interface structure. A weighting sensitivity analysis checks robustness of rankings. The framework is applied to three experimentally motivated interfaces under tensile, compressive, and shear loading.
AI.result: Bulk simulations show Shockley partial dislocations dominate plastic deformation with alloy chemistry controlling the transition to mixed-character dislocation networks. Tensile loading produces the greatest interface accommodation while shear produces minimal structural evolution. The Al9M2/Al3Ti interface shows the highest yield resistance and largest accommodation response. The interface ranking is robust to the specific form of the index used.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a transferable, quantitative approach for comparing interface accommodation in multiphase alloys. It identifies interface chemistry and crystallography as key design variables for damage-tolerant structural materials, though connection to macroscopic ductility requires experimental validation since the simulations quantify structural accommodation, not ductility or fracture directly.

title: Neural-field design of broadband Rayleigh-wave carpet cloaks under microstructure realisability constraints
summary: Transformation elasticity provides appropriate material distributions for elastodynamic cloaks but the required stiffness tensors generally violate the minor symmetries of Cauchy elasticity and are difficult to realise using conventional materials. Existing approaches restore these symmetries by modifying the transformed tensor, producing only an approximate cloak. In this work rather than modifying the transformed tensor we seek the best performing cloak within the class of Cauchy materials. We formulate 2D Rayleigh wave carpet cloak design as an optimisation problem governed by partial differential equations. Using a coordinate based neural-field and a differentiable finite element model solver we optimise symmetric stiffness and density fields by minimising wave field distortion. Both single frequency and broadband optimisation are considered, with the broadband model trained over multiple frequencies. Physical realisability is addressed using a database of homogenised microstructures through conditional diffusion, neural-field inverse design, and nearest-neighbour selection. FEM simulations show that the optimised Cauchy design approaches the ideal transformation-based cloak. After projection onto explicit microstructures, the homogenised representation recovers approximately 97% of the defect free reference surface-displacement magnitude, while direct FEM simulation of the fully resolved microstructured geometry recovers approximately 76%

AI.tldr: This paper presents an optimization-based approach for designing 2D Rayleigh wave carpet cloaks using Cauchy elastic materials (with symmetric stiffness tensors), overcoming the impracticality of transformation-based cloaks that require non-symmetric tensors. A coordinate-based neural field and differentiable FEM solver optimize stiffness and density fields to minimize wave distortion for single-frequency and broadband cases. Physical realizability is achieved via homogenized microstructure databases with conditional diffusion and neural-field inverse design.
AI.motivation: Transformation elastodynamics yields ideal cloaks but requires stiffness tensors that violate minor symmetries of Cauchy elasticity, making them very difficult or impossible to realize with conventional materials. Prior approaches sacrificed cloak fidelity by modifying the transformed tensor to restore symmetry, producing only approximate cloaks. The authors instead seek the optimal cloak directly within the physically realizable class of Cauchy materials.
AI.method: The 2D Rayleigh wave carpet cloak design is formulated as a PDE-constrained optimization problem. A coordinate-based neural field parameterizes the design (symmetric stiffness and density), and a differentiable finite element solver enables gradient-based optimization by minimizing wave field distortion. Both single-frequency and broadband (multi-frequency) training are performed. Physical realizability is handled through homogenized microstructures: conditional diffusion generates candidate microstructures, neural-field inverse design maps properties to geometry, and nearest-neighbour selection projects the optimal property fields onto discrete microstructures.
AI.result: FEM simulations demonstrate that the optimized Cauchy elastic design approaches the performance of the ideal transformation-based cloak. After projection onto explicit microstructures, the homogenized representation recovers approximately 97% of the defect-free reference surface-displacement magnitude, while direct FEM simulation of the fully resolved microstructured geometry recovers approximately 76%.
AI.conclusion: Optimization within the physically admissible Cauchy material class can produce high-performing elastodynamic cloaks without reliance on unrealistic non-symmetric stiffness tensors. The design-to-fabrication pipeline demonstrates that the performance achieved in optimization can be substantially preserved after projecting onto explicit homogenized microstructures, though a gap remains between homogenized prediction (~97%) and fully resolved simulation (~76%).

title: Remote epitaxy beyond polarity
summary: Remote epitaxy through a monolayer two-dimensional material-covered substrate establishes a crystallographic registry across the van der Waals (vdW) surface that enables the epitaxial growth, lift-off and transfer of single-crystalline films. A central belief in remote epitaxy is that the substrate facilitating the phenomenon must be a material with strong ionicity, as the interatomic electrostatic potential fluctuation in covalent and metallic materials is substantially attenuated by two-dimensional materials. Here, we show remote epitaxy is possible when the substrate is a metallic or covalently bonded material and experimentally demonstrate non-polar remote homo- and heteroepitaxy across a wide range of material systems, including both metals and semiconductors. The achieved non-polar remote interactions are designed and engineered by harnessing substrate conductivity and vicinal surface step-edge density. These findings indicate that remote epitaxy is universal and applicable to ionic, metallic, and covalent materials, expanding its capabilities and stimulating a plethora of new fundamental scientific questions about the mechanism of remote epitaxy.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that remote epitaxy, previously believed to require strongly ionic substrates, can also work with metallic or covalently bonded substrates by engineering substrate conductivity and vicinal surface step-edge density, thereby establishing remote epitaxy as a universal phenomenon applicable to ionic, metallic, and covalent materials.
AI.motivation: Remote epitaxy has been thought to require strongly ionic substrates because electrostatic potential fluctuations from covalent and metallic materials were believed to be attenuated by two-dimensional materials. The authors aim to challenge this central belief and show remote epitaxy is possible across a broader class of materials.
AI.method: The authors demonstrate non-polar remote homo- and heteroepitaxy across metals and semiconductors by designing and engineering substrate conductivity and vicinal surface step-edge density to achieve non-polar remote interactions.
AI.result: Remote epitaxy was experimentally demonstrated on metallic and covalently bonded substrates across a wide range of material systems, including both metals and semiconductors, establishing that remote epitaxy is not limited to ionic substrates.
AI.conclusion: Remote epitaxy is universal and applicable to ionic, metallic, and covalent materials, expanding its capabilities and raising new fundamental scientific questions about the underlying mechanism.

title: Customized spin spirals in ferromagnetic thin films
summary: The advancement of spintronic nanoscale devices hinges on the ability to flexibly engineer magnetic spin structures in thin-film stacks with precision and control. Meeting this demand remains a challenge for stable non-collinear spin configurations and, more specifically, vertical spin spirals in thin films. Innovative methods are required for their fabrication, stabilization and control. Here, we use oblique-incidence deposition to design and stabilize vertical spin spirals at room temperature and without an external field in magnetic thin films. We induce two crossed uniaxial magnetic anisotropies at the thin film boundaries. These anisotropies are tunable in direction and strength, thus providing control over the angular range and depth profile of the resulting spin spiral. The combination of polarized neutron reflectometry and nuclear resonant scattering enables precise and direct determination of the depth-dependent spin configurations. Our results establish a single-film design approach, in which the surface anisotropies independently serve as controllable design parameters for tailoring the vertical spin-spiral profile. Potential applications include nanoscale energy-storage devices, magnetic sensors, and ferromagnetic-resonance filters, advancing all-spin-based device engineering in general.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates a method to design and stabilize vertical spin spirals at room temperature without external magnetic fields in thin magnetic films using oblique-incidence deposition, which induces two crossed tunable uniaxial magnetic anisotropies at the film boundaries. Depth-dependent spin configurations are precisely characterized via polarized neutron reflectometry and nuclear resonant scattering, establishing surface anisotropies as controllable design parameters for spintronic device engineering.
AI.motivation: Advancing spintronic nanoscale devices requires precise engineering of magnetic spin structures in thin films, yet stabilizing non-collinear spin configurations—particularly vertical spin spirals—remains challenging. Innovative methods are needed for their fabrication, stabilization, and control.
AI.method: Oblique-incidence deposition is used to induce two crossed uniaxial magnetic anisotropies at the thin film boundaries, which are tunable in both direction and strength. The resulting vertical spin spirals are stabilized at room temperature without external fields. Depth-dependent spin configurations are directly determined using a combination of polarized neutron reflectometry and nuclear resonant scattering.
AI.result: The induced crossed uniaxial anisotropies provide control over the angular range and depth profile of the resulting spin spiral. The experimental techniques enable precise and direct determination of depth-dependent spin configurations, establishing a single-film design approach where surface anisotropies independently serve as controllable design parameters.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a single-film design approach for tailoring vertical spin-spiral profiles, with potential applications in nanoscale energy-storage devices, magnetic sensors, and ferromagnetic-resonance filters, advancing all-spin-based device engineering.

title: From Electronic Structure to Environmental Remediation: Adsorption of Ionized Glyphosate on COOH-Modified Carbon Nanotube
summary: Glyphosate is a widely used herbicide whose persistence and toxicity in aquatic and terrestrial environments demand efficient removal strategies. Here we employ GFN2 xTB calculations with implicit ALPB aqueous solvation and automated docking to investigate the adsorption of all five pH dependent ionized forms of glyphosate (G1-G5) on (10,0) single walled carbon nanotubes covalently functionalized with carboxyl groups at 0-25% coverage. Adsorption energies reveal a clear charge dependent trend: the dianionic (G4) and trianionic (G5) species exhibit the most negative binding energies over the entire functionalization range, while the protonated and neutral forms (G1, G2) bind weakly, approaching reversible adsorption at high COOH contents. The deprotonated form G5 strengthens from -2.17 eV on pristine CNT to about -5.7 eV at 10% and 25% functionalization, with a local minimum near 15-20% COOH due to steric and electrostatic crowding of adjacent groups. Decomposition of the solvation free energy shows dominant electrostatic stabilization complemented by increasingly favorable hydrogen bond contributions as carboxyl density grows. All complexes display very small HOMO-LUMO gaps (0.02-0.22 eV), indicating high electronic sensitivity to adsorption and functionalization. Overall, CNT+COOH systems can operate in both strong capture and regenerable regimes depending on glyphosate ionization state, offering a tunable platform for pH responsive remediation.
